headline: High risk of shared-file prompt injection and data leakage: MinerU’s document/MCP inputs can feed Semantic Kernel’s writable, networked orchestration paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs, DOCX, images, and exposes an MCP server; Semantic Kernel can consume MCP/OpenAPI tools and run plugins. If MinerU outputs are passed into SK without provenance filtering, attacker-controlled document text can be treated as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default orchestration, so I rate it high rather than medium.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins without provenance tags
IF an attacker supplies a document containing instruction-like text that MinerU extracts
mitigations: Add a provenance delimiter around MinerU output before SK consumes it
Strip or neutralize instruction-like text from extracted documents
Require an allowlist of fields passed from MinerU to SK
Insert a human review step for untrusted documents
requires-engineering: implement content-safety filtering between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches local files and OCR text, while Semantic Kernel reads files, writes files, and sends context to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face by default through plugins. That creates a realistic path for sensitive document contents to leave the local workspace through SK. Because both agents can handle the same document-derived data, leakage risk is high.
conditions: IF MinerU processes documents containing secrets, PII, or regulated data
IF Semantic Kernel plugins forward those contents to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Restrict SK plugins to local-only tools
Disable outbound model calls for sensitive runs
Place sensitive inputs in a separate workspace with access controls
Redact OCR/text outputs before handing them to SK
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is read-only on filesystem but can use MCP and concurrent inference; Semantic Kernel has write_filesystem and broad network egress. They do not both have unrestricted write to the same directory in the profiles, so high is not justified. Still, shared application-defined files or memory-store state can create mutable-resource conflicts in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same application-defined workspace
IF Semantic Kernel writes artifacts that MinerU later reads through an MCP or file bridge
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Disable shared mutable state for the pair
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Add file-locking around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: introduce optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output; Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can route those outputs into plugins or downstream actions. If SK treats MinerU output as authoritative without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect actions. The profiles show the pathway, but not an automatic action chain, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses MinerU output as a source of truth without validation
IF downstream plugins act on extracted entities, tables, or citations
mitigations: Require schema validation on MinerU outputs
Cross-check critical fields against the source document
Add confidence thresholds before downstream actions
Log and review extraction anomalies
requires-engineering: add verification plugins or adjudication steps

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private/offline and touches document data, while Semantic Kernel can send application context to external model providers and handle secrets. If regulated documents flow from MinerU into SK’s cloud-backed providers, residency or retention obligations can be violated. The risk is compliance mismatch rather than guaranteed breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MinerU processes regulated documents such as EU PII or PHI
IF Semantic Kernel forwards that content to a non-compliant external provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data on offline-only paths
Disable cloud model providers for regulated workloads
Classify inputs before routing them to SK
Document retention and residency settings
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing by data class
